note: The JABA abstract states that self-monitoring via activity cards increased on-schedule and on-task behavior, and that supervisor feedback was added subsequently because some staff did not maintain consistently high levels of performance. The 'evening-shift generalization' distractor is tempting because staff studies often report shift-based decrements, but the added component was prompted by a failure to MAINTAIN gains, not a generalization failure — the paper in fact reports generalization to evening hours without programming. FLAG (minor, accepted): the key is the only option naming a maintenance problem and reads close to the abstract, so the item is partly answerable by wording match. Verified against pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC1286140/.
